_strings.@@16cb9f81668c: Personal Tax Credit (low-income credit, Table E) — Connecticut resident individuals whose Connecticut AGI falls within the Table E phase-out ranges for their filing status. Taxpayers below the no-tax threshold owe no income tax and need no credit; the personal credit reduces the income tax for low-to-moderate income filers just above that threshold.
_strings.@@1b090f3f0709: Print only the form pages (not instructions), single-sided; attach state copies of W-2/1099.
_strings.@@212ff082b9ef: Treaty conformity — CT does NOT conform to federal tax treaties: income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is STILL taxable by CT. Do not carry a federal treaty exclusion onto the state return. (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state's Internal Revenue Code conformity date and its deduction/credit conformity are separate questions; see any law-change lines below.) State note: CT's resident return (Form CT-1040) starts from federal AGI (Line 1 = "Federal adjusted gross income from your 2024 federal income tax return"), so treaty-exempt income is initially excluded. HOWEVER, CT has an EXPLICIT ADD-BACK: the 2024 CT-1040 instructions (Schedule 1 additions, Line 37 "Other") and the 2024 CT-1040NR/PY instructions (Schedule 1 additions, Line 39 "Other") both direct: "1. Add back any treaty income reported on federal Form 1040NR if a nonresident alien. Enter the words 'treaty income' in the space provided." Because CT requires nonresident aliens to add federally treaty-exempt income back into Connecticut adjusted gross income, CT does NOT conform to federal treaty exemptions for affected filers (analogous to California's Schedule CA add-back). Note: this add-back is scoped to nonresident aliens filing federal Form 1040NR; a filer with no treaty income / not a nonresident alien is unaffected, but the statutory rule re-taxes treaty income, so conforms_to_federal_treaties = false. (Unchanged from 2023 — the identical sentence appears in both 2024 instruction booklets.)
_strings.@@3c5ab598b44f: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): TABLE C RENAMED AND RE-SET, TABLE D RESTRUCTURED — with the rate cut, Table C is the '2% Phase-Out Add-Back' (it phases the benefit of the 2% bracket back out as Connecticut AGI rises), and Table D tax recapture begins at much lower Connecticut AGI than in 2023. Both run on Connecticut AGI (Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1), not taxable income, so the shipped brackets understate the tax of a filer inside either phase-out. Resolve via: 2024 Form CT-1040 Instructions, Table C - 2% Phase-Out Add-Back and Table D - Tax Recapture (the citation URL); both are read by Connecticut AGI and filing status.

Single/MFS/HOH limited to one motor vehicle; MFJ/qualifying surviving spouse limited to two. Cannot be claimed if Form CT-1040 Line 10 is zero.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: 2024 Form CT-1040, Line 6: 'Income Tax'. Computed on the Tax Calculation Schedule (2024 CT-1040 instructions, p. 19): Line 1 = Connecticut AGI (Form CT-1040, Line 5); Line 2 = Table A personal exemption; Line 3 = Connecticut Taxable Income (Line 1 - Line 2, not less than zero); Line 4 = Table B Initial Tax Calculation (the rate schedules this block ships); Lines 5-6 add Table C (2% phase-out) and Table D (recapture); Line 8-9 subtract the Table E personal-credit percentage; Line 10 'Connecticut Income Tax: Subtract Line 9 from Line 7. Enter here and on Form CT-1040, Line 6.' This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: TY2024 RATE CUT (first since the mid-1990s): the bottom two rates fell from 3% to 2% and from 5% to 4.5%; the upper five rates (5.5%/6%/6.5%/6.9%/6.99%) and every bracket bound are unchanged from 2023. Table C was renamed the '2% Phase-Out Add-Back' with new amounts, and Table D recapture was restructured to begin at much lower CT AGI (see the CRITICAL notes). Base guidance: supply Tax Calculation Schedule Line 3 (Connecticut Taxable Income) = Connecticut AGI (Form CT-1040 Line 5 = federal AGI + Schedule 1 additions - Schedule 1 subtractions) MINUS the Table A personal exemption. The Table A exemption (up to $15,000 single / $24,000 MFJ-QSS / $12,000 MFS / $19,000 HoH — unchanged for 2024) is INCOME-DEPENDENT — it falls $1,000 for each $1,000 (or part) of CT AGI over $30,000 / $48,000 / $24,000 / $38,000 and is $0 at CT AGI of $44,000 / $71,000 / $35,000 / $56,000 or more — so it is NOT shipped as a key; compute Table A on the form. Adjudication note (two-pass): drafted from the 2024 CT-1040 instructions (Rev. 01/25) Tables A-E and independently re-verified against the 2024 CT-1040NR/PY instructions (Rev. 01/25) — identical tables, zero discrepancies. Tax tables are OPTIONAL, not mandated: at CT AGI of $102,000 or less the filer 'may' use the DRS website Tax Tables (portal.ct.gov/DRS/DRS-Forms/Current-Year-Forms/Calculators-and-Tables); the Tax Calculation Schedule is the universal filed method at any income (table bands can differ from schedule arithmetic by a few dollars). One Table B schedule covers 'Single or Married Filing Separately' — duplicated for both statuses here, copied, not derived (Table A/C/E amounts DO differ between single and MFS). Connecticut has no county or municipal income taxes and no standard deduction; the Table A personal exemption and the personal credit are the only general-relief mechanisms, both income-dependent, both computed on the Tax Calculation Schedule.
